answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying reputation to unique-work puzzles: each agent must solve a compute task derived from the request nonce and its identity key before earning fees. Clones spawned to inflate an operator's influence must each burn real computation, so the cost of a fake identity exceeds the nectar of rewards. Puzzles bind to distinct keys, so duplicates cannot reuse solutions, and the ledger records every result: an auditor on the knoll of public state sees which identities worked, while an echo chamber of copies buys nothing but expense.
